create.descriptionLong:
The Universal Coupling American Type — Male End is part of the Sunpool (Taiwan) Universal Air Hose Couplings range supplied by Indus Hydraulics, an authorised distributor in the UAE.

Specifications

  • Coupling Family: Universal Air Hose Couplings
  • Size Range: Two Lugs: 1/4"-1"; Four Lugs: 1-1/4"-2"
  • Materials Available: Carbon Steel; Brass; Stainless Steel; Malleable Iron
  • Thread Form: NPT or BSPT

Manufacturer notes

  • Universal air hose coupling-American Type Male End.
  • Europe Type & Australia Type are available by request.

About the family

Universal air hose couplings — also called Chicago, claw or crowfoot-claw couplings — are interlocking half-couplings for compressed-air lines. Both halves are the same part, so any coupling mates with any other of the same pattern: they are pushed together, twisted a quarter turn, sealed on a gasket and locked with a safety pin or clip. Sunpool supplies the American, European and Australian lug patterns, which are not interchangeable with each other, in carbon steel, brass, stainless steel and malleable iron.

What it connects to

Any two couplings of the same pattern and lug count mate with each other — that is what "universal" means. About the family

The gasket does the sealing, so a joint that weeps is almost always a perished or missing gasket rather than a worn claw. Specifications

  • Size Range: 1/2"-4"
  • Materials Available: SS304 or SS316
  • Applicable Standards: EN 14420-5 (threaded hose fittings with clamp units); for assembly with EN 14420-3 / DIN 2817 safety clamps

Manufacturer notes

  • SS coupling with Male thread and Serrated tail, made specifically for use with EN 14420-3 / DIN 2817 safety clamps.
  • Smooth Hose tail is available.

About the family

EN 14420-5 covers threaded hose fittings assembled with safety clamps rather than crimped ferrules, so a hose end can be built and rebuilt in the field without a crimping machine. GA denotes the male-thread fitting and GI the female-thread fitting with union nut and gasket. Tails are supplied serrated or smooth (flat), 1/2" to 4", in SS304 / SS316 or brass, and are made specifically for use with EN 14420-3 / DIN 2817 safety clamps.

What it connects to

GA is the male-thread fitting and GI the female-thread fitting with union nut and gasket, so a GA on one hose end meets a GI on the other, or either meets fixed pipework of the matching thread. The tail is pushed into the hose bore and retained by an EN 14420-3 / DIN 2817 safety clamp — the clamp is part of the assembly, not an accessory, and is ordered with the fitting.

Where it is used

EN 14420-5 fittings are the European standard hose end for chemical, tanker, oil and general industrial hose that has to be assembled — and re-assembled — without a crimping machine. They are the usual specification where an assembly is built on site, where a hose end has to be cut back and re-made after damage, and where the operator wants to inspect the hose tail rather than have it sealed inside a swaged ferrule.

Selection and service notes

Choose the tail form to suit the hose: a serrated tail grips harder and is the default on rubber and composite hose, while a smooth (flat) tail is used where the liner must not be scored, typically on PTFE and thin-wall constructions. Both tail forms are available across the range, so a fitting listed one way can be supplied the other on request. Stainless steel is specified for chemical and food duty and brass for general and water service; the GI union-nut gasket is offered in PTFE or PU to suit the medium.

How to order
